cards.text: Ezekiel is a priest, the son of Buzi (Ezekiel 1:3). He has just seen a vision of the glory of the LORD and fallen facedown (Ezekiel 1:28). Then the voice speaks: 'Son of man,' He says, 'stand up on your feet and I will speak to you.'

cards.question: As the voice speaks, the Spirit enters Ezekiel and sets him on his feet.

cards.text: Ezekiel's back on his feet. 'Son of man,' He says, 'I am sending you to the Israelites, to a rebellious nation that has rebelled against Me.'

cards.question: The LORD says Israel has been rebelling against Him. Who has been rebelling, and for how long?

answers.text: Them and their fathers to this day
Only them since the exile began
Only their kings for a few years

cards.text: He calls them obstinate and stubborn children, and He's sending Ezekiel to them. Friend, that's like being the new hire handed the one client who hangs up on EVERYBODY.

cards.question: Whether Israel listens or refuses to listen, the LORD says they will know that a ___ has been among them.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Ezekiel not to be afraid of them or their words. Not once, not twice, THREE times.

cards.question: The LORD promises Ezekiel that the people around him will be easy to live among.

cards.text: He's not to be afraid, though briers and thorns surround him and he dwells among scorpions. Some neighborhood.

cards.question: Even if Israel refuses to listen, the LORD tells Ezekiel to ___ His words to them anyway.

cards.text: Then the LORD turns to Ezekiel himself: 'Do not be rebellious like that rebellious house.'

cards.question: Right after telling Ezekiel not to be rebellious, what does the LORD tell him to do?

answers.text: Open his mouth and eat what he's given
Tear his robe and sit in the dust
Go and wash in the River Kebar

cards.text: Ezekiel looks and sees a hand reaching out to him with a scroll in it, and He unrolls it right in front of him. Friend, when somebody hands you something to eat and it's got WRITING on it, you read the label.

cards.question: The scroll is written on front and back. What kind of words are on it?

cards.text: The LORD is still holding out that scroll of woe, and He tells Ezekiel, 'Eat this scroll, then go and speak to the house of Israel.'

cards.question: When the LORD tells him to eat the scroll, Ezekiel opens his mouth and is fed the scroll.

cards.text: And this isn't a nibble, friend. 'Son of man,' He says, 'eat and fill your stomach with this scroll I am giving you.'

cards.question: That scroll is full of lamentation, mourning and woe. How does it taste in Ezekiel's mouth?

cards.text: Then the LORD sends him to the house of Israel, not to a people of unfamiliar speech or difficult language. Same language, same people, no translator needed.

cards.question: The LORD says that if He had sent Ezekiel to peoples whose words he can't understand, they would have refused to listen.

cards.text: If the LORD had sent him to peoples whose words he can't understand, they would have listened, but the LORD says the house of Israel will be unwilling to listen to him. Friend, that one stings.

cards.question: Why does the LORD say the house of Israel won't listen to Ezekiel?

answers.text: Because they won't listen to the LORD
Because Ezekiel is a stranger to them
Because his message is full of woe

cards.text: The LORD says the whole house of Israel is hard-headed and hard-hearted. Tough crowd, friend.

cards.question: The house of Israel is hard-headed and hard-hearted. What does the LORD say He'll make just as hard as theirs?
The LORD says He will make Ezekiel's forehead like a diamond, harder than flint.

cards.text: Harder than flint, friend, and MY edges went soft from years of baking cookies. Then the LORD adds, 'listen carefully to all the words I speak to you, and take them to heart.'

cards.question: The LORD tells Ezekiel to go to his own people, the ___, and speak to them.

cards.text: Then the Spirit lifts Ezekiel up, and he hears a great rumbling sound behind him: 'Blessed be the glory of the LORD in His dwelling place!'

cards.question: What's making the great rumbling sound behind Ezekiel?

answers.text: Wings and wheels of the living creatures
Hooves and chariots on the road
Voices and harps of the exiles

cards.text: A rumble that big behind ME, and I'm diving face-first into the chocolate chips. Then the Spirit takes Ezekiel away, with the strong hand of the LORD upon him.

cards.question: As the Spirit carries him off, how does Ezekiel go?

answers.text: In bitterness and anger of spirit
In gladness and joy of heart
In peace and quiet of mind

cards.text: He comes to the exiles at Tel-abib, who live by the River Kebar. For seven days he sits right where they sit.

cards.question: For seven days, Ezekiel stays among the exiles at Tel-abib, ___.

cards.text: I think that was a heavy week for Ezekiel. Stick around, friend, because his call isn't wrapped up yet.
